ground_truth.author: Rob Mardisalu
ground_truth.main_content:
⚠️ This VPN is no longer actively maintained or reviewed

This VPN service is either no longer operational or no longer meets our current testing and review standards.

For up-to-date, independently tested options, see our Recommended VPN Services.

Perfect Privacy is a recognizable name in the VPN industry.

We use several of their free privacy services to check other VPN connections and proxy servers, for instance.

But this time, we’re turning the table to see whether their encryption and protocol offerings are up to snuff.

Perfect Privacy comes courtesy of the German-based CyberDock IT Solutions GmbH, which was founded in 2008 and has been providing VPN services since then.

And in this Perfect Privacy VPN review, we’ll spill the beans on their private network, including whether you should fork over your hard-earned dough or stick to their free resources, instead.

Perfect-Privacy VPN Overview

OVERALL RANK: N/A
USABILITY: Moderate, Limited App Support
LOG FILES: No Logging Policy (Proven)
LOCATIONS: 22 countries, 55+ dedicated servers
SUPPORT: FAQ, Forum, & Email (No Live Chat)
TORRENTING: Torrenting Allowed on Most Servers
NETFLIX: Limited Success (Not Recommended for Streaming)
ENCRYPTION/PROTOCOL: AES-256, OpenVPN, IKEv2/IPSec, SSH, SOCKS5 (No WireGuard)
COST: €7.68/mo (2-year) – $8.95/mo USD equivalent
OFFICIAL WEBSITE: www.perfect-privacy.com

Perfect Privacy Pros

Perfect Privacy doesn’t let us down in several key areas, offering solid protocols and encryption options. Their logging policy is genuinely verified, connections are leak-free, and the application is functional for power users.

Here’s a detailed breakdown of their positives.

1. Industry-Standard Encryption and Protocols

Perfect Privacy starts strong, offering the OpenVPN protocol along with IKEv2/IPSec and SSH tunneling, plus SOCKS5 proxies for specialized use cases.

OpenVPN remains your best choice in most scenarios, as it provides military-grade AES-256 encryption. This encryption standard is virtually unbreakable with current technology. Even today’s most powerful supercomputers would require decades to crack through it, making your data effectively future-proof against brute force attacks.

The other protocol options serve specific purposes for different devices and use cases. For example, older devices might struggle with OpenVPN’s resource requirements, while iOS devices typically perform better with IKEv2/IPSec. However, it’s worth noting that Perfect Privacy does not yet support WireGuard protocol, which has become the modern standard for speed and efficiency among leading VPN providers.

2. Verified Zero-Logging Policy

Perfect Privacy’s no-logs policy stands out from the crowd because it has been tested in real-world conditions.

Unlike many VPN companies that use complex legal language to give themselves wiggle room, Perfect Privacy keeps their policy straightforward. This transparency becomes even more meaningful when you consider that in 2016, Dutch authorities seized two of Perfect Privacy’s servers in Rotterdam. The incident proved that no customer data was compromised, validating their no-logs claims in practice.

Many other VPN companies will use sophisticated legalese to give themselves some wiggle room. That way, users either won’t understand what they’re agreeing to, or they’ll be powerless to stop the company from using your personal data however they please.

Fortunately, you don’t have that issue with Perfect Privacy, as their commitment to privacy has been proven under real-world pressure.

3. Leak-Free and Secure Connections

We use Perfect Privacy’s free IP check to make sure each VPN connection is telling the truth.

Some VPN connections will accidentally ‘leak’ your true IP address, completely defeating the purpose of using a VPN in the first place.

So this time, we turned the tables and double-checked Perfect Privacy’s connection using multiple independent testing tools. They came out clean in each case:

https://ipleak.net/ (no leaks detected)

https://www.perfect-privacy.com/check-ip/ (no leaks detected)

https://ipx.ac/run (no leaks detected)

https://browserleaks.com/webrtc (no leaks detected)

https://www.perfect-privacy.com/dns-leaktest/ (no leaks detected)

http://dnsleak.com/ (no leaks detected)

Additionally, our security scans confirmed that their installation files are completely clean of malware or viruses.

This is reassuring news, especially considering that some VPN providers have been found to include unwanted software in their installation packages. Perfect Privacy maintains clean, secure software that won’t compromise your device’s security.

4. Functional Application with Advanced Features

Perfect Privacy’s application design prioritizes functionality over flashy aesthetics.

Their app follows a minimalist approach focused on power users who value control over simplicity:

The interface provides access to essential features including protocol selection, server switching, and advanced configuration options. Once connected, you can minimize the client to the system tray for unobtrusive operation.

We did encounter some minor limitations during testing. Server switching can take up to 30 seconds, which feels sluggish compared to instant connections offered by premium competitors. The interface design also feels dated compared to modern VPN applications available.

However, Perfect Privacy’s kill switch feature works reliably and offers three levels of protection:

Tunnel-only mode (active only when VPN is connected)

Application mode (active when software is running)

Permanent mode (works even when software is closed)

We tested this feature extensively and confirmed it works as advertised:

The kill switch effectively blocks internet access when the VPN connection drops, protecting your real IP address from exposure.

5. Adequate Customer Support

Perfect Privacy offers support through FAQ documentation, community forums, and email tickets.

Live chat support is not available, which has become a standard expectation for premium VPN services.

The FAQ section covers basic questions adequately, and the forum provides community-driven support. However, complex technical issues require email contact with their support team.

We tested their email support by submitting a query at 10:25 PM and received a response approximately 12 hours later at 10:29 AM.

The response was personal and engaged with our specific questions rather than providing generic copy-paste answers. Perfect Privacy’s support team even offers TeamViewer screen sharing for complex technical troubleshooting, demonstrating their commitment to resolving customer issues.

6. RAM-Only Server Infrastructure

Perfect Privacy operates entirely on RAM-based (diskless) servers, which provides an additional layer of security.

Unlike traditional hard drive storage, RAM-only servers cannot retain any data when powered down. This means that even if authorities seize a server, no user data can be recovered from the hardware itself. All server software and configurations are loaded fresh from secure locations when the server boots up.

This infrastructure choice aligns with Perfect Privacy’s proven commitment to user privacy and provides technical backing for their no-logs policy.

Perfect Privacy Cons

Perfect Privacy started with solid fundamentals but struggles to compete with modern VPN standards in several key areas.

Server speeds lag behind competitors, streaming support is virtually non-existent, and the limited server network creates bottlenecks during peak usage.

1. Below-Average Server Speeds

Performance testing reveals significant speed limitations with Perfect Privacy’s network.

Encryption inevitably creates some overhead, but modern VPNs have minimized this impact through optimized protocols and server infrastructure. Perfect Privacy’s speeds fall short of current industry standards.

Our baseline test without VPN showed 98.71 Mbps download and 53 Mbps upload speeds.

Connected to a Perfect Privacy server in the Netherlands:

Download: 62.21 Mbps (37% slower than baseline)

Upload: 18.62 Mbps (65% slower than baseline)

Performance degraded further when connecting to distant servers. Testing a US server in New York:

Download: 32.78 Mbps (67% slower than baseline)

Upload: 33.27 Mbps (37% slower than baseline)

These results place Perfect Privacy below the performance standards expected from premium VPN services. Leading competitors like ExpressVPN and NordVPN typically maintain much smaller speed reductions.

2. Poor Streaming Service Support

Perfect Privacy performs poorly for streaming applications, particularly with Netflix and other geo-restricted content.

Our testing across multiple Perfect Privacy servers found extremely limited Netflix compatibility:

U.S. Washington server – blocked

U.S. New York server – blocked

UK server – blocked

Canada server – blocked

Netherlands server – occasionally working

Perfect Privacy openly acknowledges that streaming is not their primary focus. Their company representative explained that they prioritize privacy features over streaming capabilities. While this approach may appeal to privacy-focused users, it limits the service’s versatility compared to competitors that successfully balance both privacy and streaming access.

If streaming is important for your VPN usage, consider alternatives from this specialized streaming VPN list.

3. Limited Server Network

Perfect Privacy maintains approximately 55 dedicated servers across 22 countries.

While this network covers major regions, the server count falls significantly short of industry leaders. NordVPN operates over 8,000 servers in 127 countries, while Private Internet Access maintains over 35,000 servers across 91 countries.

Small server networks create several practical problems:

First, higher user-to-server ratios can cause congestion during peak usage periods, leading to slower speeds and reduced reliability.

Second, limited geographic coverage means longer distances between users and servers, which increases latency and decreases performance. If Perfect Privacy doesn’t have a server near your location, you’ll experience noticeably slower speeds.

However, Perfect Privacy does use only dedicated (physical) servers rather than virtual servers, which provides better security and performance than some competitors who rely on virtualized infrastructure.

4. Jurisdiction Concerns

Perfect Privacy recently relocated from Switzerland to Germany, creating potential privacy implications.

This jurisdictional change places Perfect Privacy under German law and within the 14 Eyes intelligence-sharing alliance. While Germany has strong data protection regulations, it is part of international surveillance cooperation agreements that could theoretically impact user privacy.

The move from Switzerland (known for strong privacy protections and independence from surveillance alliances) to Germany represents a step backward in terms of jurisdictional privacy advantages. Perfect Privacy has not provided clear public explanation for this relocation.

For users requiring maximum jurisdictional privacy, VPN services based in countries like Switzerland, Panama, or Romania may offer stronger legal protections.

5. Limited Device Compatibility and App Support

Perfect Privacy offers native applications for Windows, macOS, and Android, but notably lacks an iOS app.

Supported platforms include:

Windows – native app with full features

macOS – native app with complete functionality

Android – native app available

iOS – manual configuration only (no native app)

Linux – manual setup required

Routers – custom configuration ( guide available )

Smart TVs, gaming consoles – manual setup required

The absence of an iOS app is particularly problematic, as this has become a standard offering from all major VPN providers. Perfect Privacy requires manual profile configuration on iOS devices, which is complex for average users and lacks features like the integrated kill switch.

Perfect Privacy does offer unlimited simultaneous connections, which is excellent value. However, the manual configuration requirement for many devices significantly reduces the practical benefit of this feature for non-technical users.

6. Missing Modern Protocol Support

Perfect Privacy has not yet implemented WireGuard protocol support, which has become the modern standard for VPN connections.

WireGuard offers significant advantages over older protocols:

– Faster connection speeds

– Lower battery consumption on mobile devices

– More efficient code that’s easier to audit for security

– Better performance on unstable network connections

Leading VPN providers have implemented WireGuard or WireGuard-based protocols (like NordVPN’s NordLynx) to provide superior performance. Perfect Privacy’s reliance on OpenVPN and IKEv2/IPSec, while secure, limits their competitive positioning in terms of speed and efficiency.

Perfect Privacy Plans, Pricing, and Payment Options

Perfect Privacy offers three subscription tiers with identical features but different billing periods:

1 Month – €12.99 (approximately $13.99 USD)

1 Year – saves 23% – €119.99 (approximately $129.99 USD annually)

2 Years – saves 31% – €184.14 (approximately $199.99 USD, equivalent to €7.68/$8.95 monthly)

Perfect Privacy pricing positions it among the more expensive VPN services in the market. For comparison, leading competitors offer similar or superior features at lower price points:

– NordVPN: $3.09/month (2-year plan)

– Surfshark: $1.99/month (2-year plan)

– CyberGhost: $2.19/month (2-year plan)

Payment methods include comprehensive options for various privacy preferences:

– Credit/debit cards (Visa, Mastercard, American Express)

– PayPal

– Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies

– Bank transfer

– Various regional payment processors

Perfect Privacy previously offered anonymous cash payments but discontinued this option. Bitcoin payments provide the highest level of payment anonymity currently available.

Perfect Privacy includes a 7-day money-back guarantee, which is shorter than the industry standard 30-day guarantee offered by most competitors. Importantly, refunds are not available for cryptocurrency or cash payments, limiting recourse for users who prioritize payment anonymity.

Do You Recommend Perfect Privacy?

Perfect Privacy presents a mixed value proposition in the current VPN landscape.

The service excels in core privacy fundamentals: their no-logs policy has been proven through real-world testing, they operate secure RAM-only servers, and their encryption standards are solid. For privacy-focused users who don’t require streaming capabilities, these strengths are significant.

However, Perfect Privacy struggles with modern competitive expectations. Speed performance lags behind current industry standards, their server network is notably small, and streaming service compatibility is virtually non-existent. The recent jurisdictional move from Switzerland to Germany raises questions about long-term privacy positioning.

Most concerning is the pricing structure. Perfect Privacy charges premium rates (€7.68/$8.95 monthly on 2-year plans) while delivering mid-tier performance. Leading competitors offer superior speed, larger server networks, better streaming support, and more comprehensive device compatibility at significantly lower prices.

Perfect Privacy suits a specific user profile: technically proficient individuals who prioritize proven privacy credentials over speed or streaming capabilities, and who don’t mind paying premium prices for niche features like multi-hop connections and advanced obfuscation.

For most users seeking a well-rounded VPN service, there are several alternatives that provide better overall value. Consider Perfect Privacy only if their specific privacy-focused feature set matches your exact requirements and budget allows for premium pricing.

I've tried most VPN's & Perfect Privacy is the best by a long way - The review points out it doesn't work with Netflix, this is true but a very cheap licence of Windflix sorts that out. PP's multi hop system available, no logs, whatsoever - As I live in Europe, the lack of servers doesn't affect me. Speed is pretty good for me & the VPN connects in under 10 seconds as good as most & better than some. Most people with need to add exclusions to their AV & Anti-Malware as this can cause slow connecting. If you want a all singing all dancing (cheap) VPN look elsewhere - if you want the most secure VPN there is, buy Perfect Privacy, you won't regret it - And ignore most of the VPN review sites they are sponsored, ever wonder why Nord & Express VPN always come out on top?

The BEST for privacy and anonymity

In fact, if you go to the prices page, it says that for ALL plans, FULL FUNCTIONALITY is included. There is no torrenting restrictions regardless of which plan you choose. You get access to all Perfect Privacy has to offer.

Perfect Privacy is the best when it comes to privacy. And even though they are in a cooperative jurisdiction (Switzerland), their servers use RAMDISK mode, meaning that as soon as power is disconnected, all data is lost that is on it anyway. And the fact that they log nothing paired with that means that there is zero risk of your data being exposed. I would rate them as perfect, but since Netflix only works on the "London 2" and Netherlands servers, I knocked off a bit. I simply switch to ExpressVPN when I need Netflix in another region, but it isn't too important to me.

Great VPN. Privacy is important and they nailed it.
